answer: Radio distance-bounding costs each fake identity one $40 beacon on its own site at least 2 km from any other. Three verifier stations on a ridge send random nonces; the beacon must echo each within a round-trip that fixes its range, and the three ranges triangulate one point below the horizon. Two aliases sharing a beacon or rooftop resolve to the same spot and both are rejected; a falcon-fast relay cannot beat light speed, so faking distance fails the timing. Sites cannot be shared, parallelized or bulk-bought: 100 fakes need 100 rented locations and 100 beacons.
